name: og-29-endogenous-autocatalysis
gate_reason: Gate A keystone, C6 universe: formose-type autocatalysis (linear C≤6) refuted with mechanism — the canonical doubling step r409 (2 glycolaldehyde ⇌ threose) is condensation-favored (ΔG° = −16.4 kJ/mol), so the autocatalytic splitting direction carries no net flux across the x1–x50 feed sweep (motifs = 0, gain = 0 everywhere, including x20 where the network is connected and fixing carbon). Branched C6 rTCA is under active test (branched-skeleton v2 build). Carbon fixation at C6 is network persistence (A1), not self-amplification (A2).
title: Endogenous Autocatalysis
claim: Vent-fed chemistry, assembled from the study-28 atlas reactions under the study-27 interface feeds, either forms a genuinely balanced, mass-conserving autocatalytic cycle whose amplification beats a matched null with equal chemical input fluxes — or it does not, in which case the study names the specific missing precursor or rate-limiting mechanism. Spontaneous network amplification is a claim won against a null, never inferred from apparent growth.
question: Can vent-fed chemistry spontaneously form network amplification or self-maintaining cycles — genuine, balanced autocatalysis rather than accumulation driven by the input feed?
hypothesis: Given the 27 interface feeds and the 28 reaction set, stoichiometric autocatalysis detection plus kinetic simulation under dilution will reveal whether a self-amplifying cycle exists; if it does, its amplification and net carbon fixation exceed a matched null (identical input fluxes, autocatalytic topology removed) and persist above a critical dilution rate; if it does not, the analysis isolates the missing precursor or rate-limiting step.
objective: Assemble vent-fed reaction networks from the 27 and 28 handoff bundles, detect stoichiometric autocatalysis, simulate kinetics with dilution, and test any detected amplification against a matched null — reporting either genuine autocatalysis with its critical dilution, or a clean negative that names the gap.
proposed_mechanisms: network amplification / self-maintaining cycles seeded from atlas reactions
stoichiometric autocatalysis (a subnetwork that produces its own catalyst/seed)
dilution as the selective pressure separating true autocatalysis from feed-driven accumulation
proposed_models_methods: RDKit rule-generated reaction candidates + curated atlas alternatives [to-build: reaction-rule-generation / viva_reaction_atlas]
stoichiometric autocatalysis detection on the reaction network (algebraic, pre-kinetic)
COPASI/libRoadRunner kinetic simulation with dilution                 [in-workspace: viva_genesis.protometabolism]
discrete/stochastic kinetics where expected molecule counts make continuum concentrations unreliable (evidence standard
eQuilibrator ΔG screen so any detected cycle is thermodynamically allowed [exists: viva_equilibrator]
matched-null construction + PyMC/SALib sensitivity & identifiability   [partial: viva_genesis.uq]

model_approach.prose: Study 29 is the chemical-emergence test. It assumes no amplification; it consumes the 27 feeds and 28 reactions as given typed bundles, detects candidate autocatalytic cycles stoichiometrically (before any kinetics), then simulates them under dilution. The decisive control is the matched null — the same chemical input fluxes with the autocatalytic coupling removed — and only amplification that beats that null counts as autocatalysis. Low-count intermediates are simulated with discrete kinetics so a handful of molecules is never mistaken for a continuum concentration.

gate_A: Gate A (chemical emergence) = studies 27 + 28 + 29 passing together. Its acceptance REQUIRES that 29's detected autocatalysis beats the matched null with chemical input fluxes held equal; without the null-beating margin, Gate A does not pass regardless of raw amplification.
decision_test: Detect genuine balanced autocatalysis — a mass-conserving cycle whose amplification and net carbon fixation beat a matched null with equal input fluxes and persist above a critical dilution — OR identify the specific missing precursor/mechanism. A clean negative is a result; apparent growth that does not separate from the matched null is NOT autocatalysis and is reported as such (evidence standard #5, #8).

config.title: Autocatalysis under flow — and the Gate-A null test
config.caption: Net carbon flux and the autocatalytic gain of the vent-fed network under flow, then the Gate-A comparison against a degree-preserving matched null run at identical input fluxes. Plainly: is the network fixing and multiplying carbon, and does that amplification beat a look-alike control fed exactly the same — or was the apparent growth just the feed?

key_assumptions: Autocatalysis must be stoichiometrically balanced — an apparent cycle fed by an untracked source is rejected, not counted.
A matched non-concentrating / non-autocatalytic null is the control the favourable case must beat.
expert_questions: Is an honest negative (a named missing precursor/mechanism) an acceptable decision outcome here, or must a positive autocatalytic cycle be demonstrated to pass?

autocatalysis-beats-matched-null.detail: At max_carbons=6 the favorable network ignites at x20 feed (network_connected=1, net_carbon_flux 5.69e-4, carbon-fixing) but autocatalytic_gain=0 and n_autocatalytic_motifs=0; the matched null at x20 has gain=0 and essentially identical flux (5.70e-4). Favorable does NOT beat the degree- preserving matched null. REFUTED for formose-type (linear C<=6).

stoichiometric-autocatalysis-detection.detail: No stoichiometric autocatalytic motif detected at any feed, including the ignited x20 point (n_autocatalytic_motifs=0 throughout). The linear C<=6 formose network fixes carbon but contains no self-amplifying cycle.

negative-result-isolates-gap.detail: Gap isolated and characterized: the linear formose universe (C<=6) has no autocatalytic motif even with an active network; the branched C6 rTCA cycle (citrate/isocitrate) is outside the v1 linear-skeleton representation and is the named v2 follow-up.

limitations: Autocatalysis discriminator result (C6): formose-type (linear C≤6) refuted, with mechanism. The canonical formose doubling step is present in the universe (r409: 2 glycolaldehyde [X_DH] ⇌ threose [X_DOOH], a coefficient-2 splitting), so this is not detector blindness or an absent motif. Its ΔG° is −16.4 kJ/mol toward condensation, so under vent feeds net flux runs the building direction (2 C2 → C4) while the autocatalytic splitting direction (C4 → 2 C2) is +16.4 kJ/mol uphill and carries no net flux across the x1–x50 feed sweep — motifs = 0 and gain = 0 everywhere, including x20 where the network is connected and fixing carbon. Formose-type does not self-amplify because the doubling step runs the wrong way at vent conditions. Branched C6 rTCA (citrate/isocitrate) is outside the v1 linear-skeleton representation and is under active test via the branched-skeleton v2 build.

Persistence is QUALIFIED by feed plausibility. The network ignites only at x20 (supply_H2 20 mM, supply_CO2 40 mM); at the vent-posterior operating point (x1) and x5 it does not ignite, and x50 washes out - a narrow window well ABOVE defensible vent feeds. Lost City dissolved H2 is ~1-15 mmol/kg (posterior example 10.8), so x20's 20 mM is ~1.3x over the H2 window; the DIC posterior is ~1.2-2.9 mM (example 1.4), so x20's 40 mM CO2 is ~14x over the DIC upper bound. So the carbon-fixing network emerges only above vent-realistic concentrations; at defensible vent feeds it does not ignite. (The autocatalysis refutation is unaffected - at the ignition point there is still 0 gain.)

The autocatalytic gain is 0 for both the vent-fed network and its matched null across the x1–x50 feed sweep, and with the C6 universe built this is a genuine, mechanistically-explained result — not a truncation artifact. The canonical doubling step (r409) is representable and present; it simply runs toward condensation (ΔG° −16.4 kJ/mol) at vent conditions, so the splitting direction that would drive self-amplification carries no net flux. The one case still outside scope is the reductive TCA cycle, whose branched C6 species the v1 linear skeleton cannot hold — the branched-skeleton v2 is being built now to test it. A coefficient-independent functional discriminator (seed-dependence + super-linear production) is also being built so formose and rTCA are judged on the same footing. So the negative is mechanistic for formose-type and an open, actively-building test for branched rTCA — not a claim that vent-fed chemistry cannot self-amplify by any route.
